Simple. The defendants are claiming their assets forfeiture system cannot produce a cash balance report without making said same system unusable by the department for several days. Despite the absurdity of the defendants claim I’d grant them this complexity excuse for the portion of their system that writes and retrieves records, but not for the portion that stores those records; the database. See, these are two wholly autonomous components, two separate pieces of software and machinery that communicate via an industry standardized language. They only interact when the portion that writes and reads records wants to write or read from the part that stores the records.

This portion of plaintiff’s system is not bespoke made and so can be accessed independently of the other parts. With a copy of the defendants database plaintiff’s expert witness can use this standardized language to run a cash balance report without needing the “complex” custom portion that NYPD claims is the reason they cannot provide the evidence in the first place.
